newsitem.title: USA: CBOT directors vote against wheat delivery changes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT directors vote against wheat delivery changes.

text.p: The Board of Directors of the Chicago Board of Trade on Wednesday voted against recommending proposed changes in the CBOT wheat delivery system for a membership vote, the exchange said in a release.
"The Board directed that further staff-level research be conducted to re-examine the existing wheat contract specifications and potential modifications to those specifications," the release stated.

The proposal called for expanding Toledo's deliverable storage space, allowing delivery from off-water warehouses in St. Louis and changing the Toledo differential to par from -2 cents. The plan would also change the delivery instrument to a shipping certificate instead of a warehouse receipt.
A shipping certificate proves the firm making delivery can get the specified amount of grain to a delivery point while a warehouse receipt confirms the grain is already in an approved warehouse.
CBOT members on Tuesday voted two to one in favor of another plan to change the corn and soybean delivery system.
